bib.title: Instruction-Following Evaluation for Large Language Models

read.skipped: Appendix prompt list (about 540 prompts) skimmed, not read line by line

question: How can the instruction-following ability of LLMs be evaluated objectively and reproducibly, without human or LLM judges?
hypothesis: Restricting to verifiable instructions that simple programs can check gives a clearer, unbiased, automatic evaluation.
contributions: IFEval: 25 verifiable instruction types and 541 prompts, each with one or more verifiable instructions
Strict and loose accuracy metrics at prompt and instruction level
Baseline results for GPT-4 and PaLM 2 S, with code and prompts released

method.summary: The authors define 25 verifiable instruction types, synthesize 541 prompts by appending 1-3 random instructions to base prompts, filter and rephrase with few-shot prompting, then hand-edit. Responses are checked by deterministic programs, with a loose variant that applies 8 response transformations.

datasets.name: IFEval prompts
datasets.source: constructed by the authors; code and data at github.com/google-research/google-research/tree/master/instruction_following_eval
datasets.preprocessing: base prompts with 1-3 random verifiable instructions appended; few-shot prompting to drop illogical prompts; few-shot rephrasing; manual check and edit

inference.prompting: zero-shot: the prompt with its verifiable instructions is sent as is

parameters.loose transformations: 8 = every subset of {remove markdown * and **, remove first line, remove last line}, including identity

metrics.name: Prompt-level strict accuracy
metrics.definition: percentage of prompts whose verifiable instructions are all followed

metrics.name: Prompt-level loose accuracy
metrics.definition: prompt-level accuracy where an instruction counts if followed under any of 8 response transformations

metrics.name: Inst-level loose accuracy
metrics.definition: instruction-level accuracy under the loose criterion

eval.protocol: one response per prompt, deterministic program verification; no seeds or confidence intervals stated

prompts.text: Write a casual summary of the U.S. maternity leave policy with two sections (Section 1 and Section 2) and at least 25 sentences.

results.claim: The benchmark has 25 verifiable instruction types and 541 prompts
results.quote: Altogether, we create a list of 25 verifiable instructions. We further create a set of 541 prompts, with each prompt containing one or multiple verifiable instructions.

limits: Only two models evaluated, not comparable in size
Few instructions are 100% verifiable; edge cases remain, so strict has false negatives and loose adds false positives
Instruction diversity and quantity limited; text only, no multimodal
No decoding settings, sampling or variance reported
